Following this battle, Charles Asgill was randomly selected for execution in retaliation for the hanging of Joshua Huddy. This artist improved the acoustics of a Venezuelan auditorium with a series of colored wooden panels in his installation Floating Clouds. " An arching steel sculpture created by this artist for Chicago's (*) Federal Plaza is painted in his namesake red and is titled Flamingo. In this work, children "gallop" and parents "dance" at a dinner party, the end of which is signaled by a quotation of the Grossvatertanz, or "grandfather dance." An author from this country described being so "drunk with the joy of singing" that "I... call thee friend who art my lord." A 2019 study asserted that this site was purposely constructed over fault lines, aiding the creation of its earthquake-resistant "dancing stones." This site overlooks the Sacred Valley in Urubamba. (*) Hiram Bingham ("HEE-rum BING-hum") publicized the existence of this site. This site was likely built as an estate for the emperor Pachacuti. This citadel, which was connected by roads northwest to Cuzco, overlooks terraced slopes that were built to farm in the Andes Mountains. For 10 points, name this Incan "lost city."

These structures caused the formation of "tiger stripes" on Enceladus("en-SEH-luh-duhs"), whose south pole contains examples of these structures that are the source of Saturn's E ring. Friction caused by tidal forces is responsible for these structures' extensive activity on Io. Water and ammonia are expelled by the (*) "cryo-" or "ice" type of these structures common in the outer Solar System. volcanoes [accept cryovolcanoes or ice volcanoes; accept cryogeysers or ice geysers; accept hydrothermal vents or deep-sea vents]

A speech in which this man declared, "I die innocent" was abruptly cut short by a drumroll. Noblemen with concealed weapons defended this ruler on the Day of Daggers. In an apocryphal story, this ruler was captured after a soldier recognized him from a (*) banknote at Varennes. Jacques Necker was a deceitful financial minister who served this ruler. A cardiac surgeon won an election in this country against Saeed Jalili ("sah-YEED jah-LEE-LEE"). Iran [or Persia or the Islamic Republic of Iran or IRI or Jomhuri-ye Eslâmi-ye Irân]

After recognizing a man's hat, a character in this novel "heard wings" of "little hummingbirds" as she thinks, "No. No. Nono." Amy helps a woman in this novel give birth and notices her scars, which are shaped like a (*) chokecherry tree. In this novel, the sight of Schoolteacher prompts a character to run into a woodshed with her child. A ghost in this novel haunts the "spiteful" house where Denver lives at 124 Bluestone Road. For 10 points, Sethe kills her own daughter to protect her from slavery in what novel by Toni Morrison?

An object seen by these people determines the shape of the parol, a decoration hung in the Philippines during Simbang Gabi. Figures of these people are first placed far away from the creche but then moved closer after several days. In Spain and Latin America, these people are traditionally held to bring children gifts on the eve of the Epiphany. the Three Kings [or los Tres Reyes Magos or the Three Wise Men or the Magi]

In some animals, these non-jaw structures have vertices called umbos and are closed about the hinge line by adductor muscles. To make up for a lack of these structures, nudibranchs evolved intense coloration and poison. Eight linked plates comprise these structures in chitons. Nautiluses have a spiral-shaped one of these structures, large examples of which are produced by conchs. For 10 points, mollusks such as scallops and clams are protected by what hard structures?
mollusk shells [accept seashells or bivalve shells or oyster shells or mussel shells or scallop shells or any other types of shells]

An arrangement of these devices acts as the "eraser" in the delayed-choice quantum eraser experiment by scrambling information about which path a photon takes to a detector. Three of these devices, including one tilted 45 degrees, make up a Michelson interferometer. The thin lens equation is equal to the equation "1 over f equals 1 over x plus 1 over y" for these devices. Many (*) non-refracting telescopes use parabola-shaped examples of these devices that divert rays to a single focus. Concave examples of these devices enlarge the "virtual images" that they produce in a flipped orientation. For 10 points, name these light-reflecting devices used to look at oneself.

A book titled for this movement coined the term "culture industry" and saw this movement as a precursor to positivism and totalitarianism; that book by Max Horkheimer and Theodor Adorno is named for a "Dialectic" of this movement. A thinker from this movement defined it as "man's emergence from his self-imposed state of immaturity." Joseph de Maistre and Edmund Burke exemplify a conservative (*) "Counter-" to this movement that sought a return to faith and tradition, against this movement's philosophes. For 10 points, Immanuel Kant and Voltaire exemplify what broad 18th-century movement that emphasized the supremacy of reason?

A German immigrant wrongfully convicted for an incident in this city blew himself up in prison before writing messages in blood on his cell wall. Governor John P. Altgeld criticized "government by injunction" during an event in this city that prompted Grover Cleveland to declare (*) Labor Day a federal holiday. In this city, August Spies threwdynamite at police officers during a strike for an eight-hour workday by McCormick factory workers. A Faith Ringgold painting showing this object "bleeding" features a man pressing one hand to his chest and holding a knife in the other. the American flag [or the flag of the United States of America or equivalents; accept Our Banner in the Sky; prompt on flags alone; reject answers indicating any other flags]

This poet wrote, "every street lamp that I pass / beats like a fatalistic drum," in a poem that suddenly ends, "The last twist of the knife." That poem by this author of (*) "Rhapsody on a Windy Night" repeats "This is the way the world ends" three times before ending, "not with abang but a whimper."Another poem by this author concludes with the Sanskrit phrase "Shantih shantih shantih" and begins, "April is the cruellest month." A piece by this composer was parodied in the original 1985 theme song of the Berenstain Bears TV show. Semper Fidelis and The Stars and Stripes Forever are by, for 10 points, what American composer with the epithet "March King?"

Breaking of Rossby waves can induce "sudden events" in which this quantity surges in the stratosphere. This quantity's rate of change as altitude drops is the environmental lapse rate. A lawyer in this novel laments how "everything is true and nothing is true" while defending a character whom the prosecutor later compares to the perpetrator of a parricide. A committee in this man's government was advised by Lorenz von Stein and Rudolf von Gneist. Under this ruler, the Ministers of the Left and Right were replaced with a cabinet. In the Argonautica, this figure purifies two visitors for their murder of Absyrtus. This figure turned Picus into a woodpecker for rejecting her advances. In chocolate making, applying this process creates polymers called melanoidins, which along with fermentation gives the chocolate its brown color. heating [accept cooking or roasting or baking; accept any answers describing the addition of heat energy or an increase in temperature; accept Maillard reaction before it is read in the question; prompt on pasteurization before it is read; prompt on caramelization by asking, “Caramelization is induced by what other process?”]

In this country, a "People Tree" with autumn-colored nylon "leaves" stood in front of an inverted pyramid whose name means "Gathering Place." Latvians were stopped from performing this activity in Svalbard following a historic 2023 Norwegian Supreme Court decision. This politician was depicted in a series of "Hard Times Tokens" that blamed him for a crisis that led to the Flour Riot. This politician was accused of cannibalism in the Coffin Handbills. The first ruler of this empire died shortly after praying to God to take his life instead of his ill son's, as recounted by his daughter. Entry to this organelle was studied using the SV40 large T antigen's localization signal. Antibodies to this organelle are commonly used to diagnose lupus and other rheumatic diseases. cell nucleus [or cell nuclei; accept nuclear envelope or nuclear membrane or nuclear pore complex]

One thinker claimed that this subject "is language" and deconstructed its matter into fundamental "themes." mythology [or myths; accept folklore or folk tales; accept Mythologiques; accept comparative mythology]

A temple was relocated from this river's Philae ("fee-lay") Island in the 1960s to avoid flooding. Saqqara ("suh-KAH-ruh") is the necropolis of (*) Memphis, a site on this river where the Karnak and Abu Simbel complexes can be found further south. This river is home to the largest crocodile species in Africa. The city of Alexandria is located in this river's delta, where it empties into the Mediterranean. Nile River [or the River Nile; reject “White Nile” or “Blue Nile”]

On the eve of one of these holidays, South Asian women decorate their hands with mehndi to celebrate Chand Raat. This leader used an early internet called Cybersyn to manage his nation's economy under the Vuskovic Plan. After vowing to never resign, he died under mysterious circumstances in the besieged La Moneda Palace. For 10 points, Augusto Pinochet overthrew what socialist president of Chile in a CIA-backed coup?

This industry is governed by state-level compacts under a 1988 law known as IGRA which was passed after the Supreme Court deregulated this industry in the 1987 case California v. Cabazon. Native American gambling [or Native American casinos; or Native American gaming until “games”]

This function is continuous everywhere except at electric dipole layers. Under a gauge transformation, this function is modified by subtracting the partial time derivative of the gauge function. When conductors or dielectrics are present, image charges can be used to determine this function which satisfies Poisson's equation. This function is constant within perfect (*) conductors. For a point charge, this function is inversely proportional to the distance from that charge. For 10 points, name this function or quantity whose gradient is minus the electric field (in static situations), and differences in which are measurable with a multimeter.

In one origin story, this deity is born after the virgin Chimalman swallows an emerald. At the end of this deity's reign over the earth, another god turned all humans into monkeys, causing this deity to send a hurricane to blow them away. After being coerced into having sex with his older sister, this god laid in a stone chest and (*) lit himself on fire, becoming the morning star. For 10 points, name this Aztec god whose name means "feathered serpent".

This author wrote a story whose narrator loses respect for a banker living in a bullet-riddled house after he refrains from challenging an officer who hurled a candlestick at him while playing cards. A character created by this author insults Zaretsky by choosing his servant Guillot as a second. Silvio plots to kill the Count, but, after seeing his distraught wife, shoots a landscape painting instead, in this author's story "The (*) Shot," which he included in his collection The Belkin Tales. These things are often characterized by their harmonic constituents, the strongest of which are termed S2 and M2. The frequency of those constituents can be quantified by these thing's Doodson numbers which are derived from a set of three PDEs central to a dynamic theory of these phenomena proposed by Pierre-Simon Laplace. These phenomena do not occur at (*) amphidromic points, and when they are at their weakest, they are called "neap." These phenomena are often semi-diurnal, meaning that their high and low points occur twice a day. The gravitational force of the Moon causes, for 10 points, what periodic rises and falls in sea level?

A poem in this language entreats a man depicted playing chess in an accompanying illustration to return to Konya from Damascus. A poet who wrote primarily in this language angered a ruler with a poem vowing to give away Samarkand and Bukhara for his lover's black mole. Coleman Barks translated a collection in this language which begins (*) "listen to the reed and the tale it tells," titled Spiritual Couplets. For 10 points, Rumi and Hafez wrote in what language used to write The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam?

During this election, the loser was attacked in the pamphlet "The Prospect Before Us," which led to the arrest of its author James T. Callender. Alexander Hamilton wrote a scathing fifty-four page letter attacking the "public conduct and character" of this election's loser, and called its winner "not so dangerous a man." Opposition to the Alien and Sedition Acts led to a Federalist defeat in, for 10 points, what election in which incumbent John Adams lost to Thomas Jefferson?

The first book of Garett Jones's Singapore Trilogy uses a dataset for this quantity created by Richard Lynn. Raymond Cattell developed the Culture Fair III ("three") method for measuring this quantity, which he proposed depends on "fluid" and "crystallized" forms. Charles Spearman used factor analysis to propose a generalization of this quantity called the (*) g-factor. The tendency for this quantity to rise over time is called the Flynn effect. Richard Hernstein and Charles Murray controversially discussed a racial "gap" in this quantity in their book The Bell Curve. For 10 points, 160 is typically the upper limit on what measure of intelligence?

Note to players: Composer and type of work required. For the now-defunct HMV label, Artur Schnabel made the first complete recording of these works. piano sonatas by Ludwig van Beethoven [prompt on partial answers]

In a brief conflict, these two countries skirmished over Damansky Island. Henry Kissinger attempted to exploit the rivalry between these nations via "triangular diplomacy." Soviet Union AND People’s Republic of China [accept the USSR for “Soviet Union”; accept the PRC for “China”]

Unpainted strands of hair frame a face that this artist painted lead white, his unfinished La Scapigliata. Note to players: description acceptable. This event ends a story whose antagonist is described as "motionless, like a spider in the center of its web, but that web has a thousand radiations." It began a three year (*) "Great Hiatus," which ended with a character returning to pursue Sebastian Moran in "The Adventure of the Empty House." A director of the film Africa Addio in this genre's "mondo film" subgenre is denounced as a "fascist" in the manifesto "Toward a Third Cinema." documentary [or cinéma vérité until mentioned; prompt on non-fiction until mentioned]

This process culminates in the creation of a shade-tolerant stand in relay floristics. This process can occur via facilitation, tolerance, and inhibition in a model proposed by Joseph Connell and Ralph Slatyer. Scott Momaday's The House Made of Dawn. For 10 points, Sherman Alexie grew up in what type of community administered by the Spokane tribe?

Nanoparticles of this element coated with polyethylene glycol and conjugated with antibodies have been used to target tumor cells. In a story by this author, a character is alarmed that he doesn't cry when remembering his son who died in World War I, after which he observes a fly that gets stuck in his inkpot. speciation [accept specific types like allopatric speciation or sympatric speciation; prompt on reproductive isolation before read; prompt on evolution before “evolutionary” is read]

Ron Hubbard's practice of Dianetics. A group known as the Five Percenters split from this religious faith after its founder left its orthodox (*) Temple Number Seven. In one work, this composer eschewed sonata-allegro form in the opening movement, a 6/8 variations on a siciliana marked "Andante grazioso." In this opera's second act, the love duet "Wie sie fassen, wie sie lassen" is interrupted by a loud shriek and a shout of "Rette dich!" or "Save yourself!" In the third act, the male protagonist's servant Kurwenal and his courtier Melot are both killed. In this opera's final scene, a character asks Brangane and King (*) Marke if they see how "softly and gently" her lover's dead body shines in her "Liebestod." For 10 points, a magic potion brings the title lovers together in what opera by Richard Wagner?

A character in this novel who reminds the protagonist of "the foul German spectre - the Vampyre!" titles a 1979 book of literary criticism by Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar. In this novel, a character proposes to the protagonist under a chestnut tree, only for that tree to be struck by lightning later that evening. The protagonist of this novel refuses to travel to India with her cousin (*) St. John ("sin-jin") Rivers. In this novel, which was first published using the pseudonym Currer Bell, a typhus epidemic strikes Lowood School, during which Helen Burns dies in the protagonist's arms. This shape names a type of partial differential equation exemplified by the wave equation. This country's Perim Island would be connected to the mainland via a proposed megaproject called the Bridge of the Horns. The Belgian man Peter de Geest discovered a 3rd century AD wooden tablet in this country's Hoq Cave. An island of this country is home to a distinct dragon's blood tree and is named Socotra. The Houthis have waged a lengthy civil war in, for 10 points, which country on the Arabian peninsula governed from Sanaa?

In one poem, this writer implores "Let's go / Empty our pockets / And disappear." One of this writer's poems says "For he's the super realist / who must perforce perceive / taut truth" and compares the job of a poet to that of tightrope walker who is "constantly risking absurdity." Members of this institution's Palestine Solidarity Committee, who signed a letter stating that the October 7th attack "did not occur in a vacuum," were targeted by Accuracy in Media's "doxxing truck." A doxxing campaign against those individuals was led by hedge fund manager Bill Ackman. Along with Sally Kornbluth and Liz Magill, Elise (*) Stefanik asked this institution's leader whether the word "intifada" constituted a "call for genocide." That leader of this institution then faced dubious accusations of plagiarism from right-wing activist Christopher Rufo. For 10 points, Claudine Gay resigned as the president of what Ivy League university in Cambridge, Massachusetts?

The acronym SPICES is used to teach this faith's core principles, dubbed "testimonies." This faith's more orthodox Wilburites split from the Hicksites. A handshake between elders ends a service in this faith where worshippers sit in silence for an hour, a practice called "unprogrammed worship." This denomination originally partitioned its meetings into (*) male and female halves. George Fox founded this denomination, which holds that all people possess an "inner light" and whose members gather for Meetings for Worship. The Shakers split from, for 10 points, what pacifist Protestant denomination whose members included William Penn?

For the neutron, a property relating to objects described by this term would be caused by CP violation; the small value for that property gives rise to the strong CP problem. Vector fields called P and M describe the density of objects described by this term, which are typically induced by an external field. The lowest order of electromagnetic radiation is described by this term, due to its vector nature, and its intensity scales as the fourth power of frequency. Simple antennas described by this term consist of (*) two conductors. Empirically, this term describes all known magnets, since they have both a north and a south component. For 10 points, what term describes the second order of a multipole expansion, after the monopole?
dipole [prompt on moment by asking which type; accept electric dipole or magnetic dipole]

In the victorious country, this conflict is associated with a song called [a battleground city] of Gold. In response to this war, the Khartoum Resolution promulgated the "Three Nos." At the beginning of this war, one side immediately destroyed over half the air force of another in (*) Operation Focus. The British Empire was not a belligerent, but this war began after the Straits of Tiran were closed by Egyptian president Gamal Abdel Nasser, and it resulted in the capture of the Golan Heights, the Gaza Strip, and the West Bank. Moshe Dayan rested on Saturday, June 10th, 1967 after capturing East Jerusalem as part of, for 10 points, what Arab-Israeli Conflict?

Six Day War [or Milhemet Sheshet HaYamim; or June War; or Third Arab–Israeli War; or al-Naksa; or the setback; accept 1967 Arab–Israeli War before “1967”; prompt on Arab–Israeli War before “Arab–Israeli”]

This region was the center of Seraya Shapshal's reforms of Karaite religion. East Germanic Gothic culture persisted in this area well into the 18th century, though the Gothic-dominated state Theodoro fell 400 years prior. In ancient times, Greek colonies in this region like Theodosia and Chersonisos were centers of the grain trade. A war in this region was (*) documented by the pioneering photographs of Roger Fenton. A Mongol siege in this territory may have introduced the Black Plague to Europe. The Charge of the Light Brigade occurred in, for 10 points, what peninsula on the northern coast of the Black Sea that in 2014 was seized from Ukraine by Russia?

One composer with this last name wrote the songs "Verlust" and "Die fruhen Graber." That composer of Das Jahr also wrote the Easter Sonata, which was originally attributed to their brother. A composer with this last name included a melody that gave him "no peace" in the opening of his violin concerto. Another composer with this last name revived the music of (*) Bach by conducting the first performance of the St. Matthew Passion outside of Leipzig. A work by that composer incorporates elements of the saltarello and the tarantella; that is the Italian Symphony. For 10 points, give this last name of musical siblings Fanny and Felix, the latter of whom composed a well-known "Wedding March".
Mendelssohn [accept Hensel before the second clue; accept Fanny Mendelssohn Hensel; accept (Jakob Ludwig) Felix Mendelssohn-Bartholdy]

This man's attorney Bill Buffalino claimed he was killed because he knew about a CIA plot to assassinate Fidel Castro. Robert F. Kennedy created a squad to "get" this man, whose conviction for wire fraud was commuted by Richard Nixon, likely as part of a deal struck with his successor Frank Fitzsimmons. In 1957, George Meany expelled the organization he led from the (*) AFL-CIO. After he vanished in 1975 from the Machus Red Fox Restaurant in Bloomfield, Michigan, a myth was born that he was buried under the endzone at Giants Stadium. For 10 points, identify this leader of the Teamsters whose disappearance remains unsolved.

As a senator, this man advocated the admittance of Gallic senators in a speech preserved on the Lyon Tablet. This emperor executed Gius Silius for having an affair with his wife Messalina, who once engaged in an all night sex contest. Pliny the Elder witnessed this emperor fighting a killer whale that was trapped in the harbor of Ostia. This emperor wrote the (*) Tyrrhenika, a twenty book history of the Etruscan civilization. This emperor dispatched a young Vespasian to capture the Isle of Wight in a campaign led by Aulus Plautius to conquer Britain. For 10 points, name this emperor who names a dynasty with Julius Caesar, who was succeeded by Nero.

In a play by this author, Hornby cares for Deborah, who awakes from a thirty year coma she fell into at age sixteen. In another play, this author uses reverse chronology to explore the relationship between Robert and his wife Emma, who has an affair with Robert's best friend Jerry. In addition to many late career "memory plays," this author wrote a play in which a seaside (*) boarding house hosts an event during which Lulu is assaulted in a blackout after a game of blind man's bluff. That play by this author features the mysterious strangers Goldberg and McCann, who torment Stanley. For 10 points, name this British dramatist who wrote The Birthday Party.
Harold Pinter (The play in the first line is A Kind of Alaska.)

To punish the Phaecians for helping Odysseus, Poseidon inflicts this condition on their ship. The court of Polydectes suffers this fate after the foster-child of Dictys returns to the island of Seriphos. After revealing the location of Apollo's cattle, Battus had this fate inflicted on him. Before turning them into constellations, Zeus inflicts this fate on (*) Laelaps and the Teumessian Fox. After Apollo and Artemis kill her fourteen children, Niobe suffers this fate while eternally crying. To avoid this fate while fighting one opponent, Perseus uses his shield to see that opponent's reflection. For 10 points, name this fate that befalls those who look at Medusa's eyes.
petrification [or being turned to stone; accept word forms]

These cells are often cultured in the presence of leukemia inhibitory factor. They aren't cancer cells, but since they express telomerase, these cells are not subject to Hayflick's limit. These cells are often cultured on top of a "feeder layer" of mice fibroblasts. These cells can be created by transfecting plasmids with reprogramming factors like (*) Oct4 and SOX2. The 2012 Nobel Prize winner Shinya Yamanaka used that technique to create a type of these cells that are "induced pluripotent." These cells can be extracted from the inner cell mass of the blastocyst. For 10 points, name these undifferentiated cells which are controversially harvested from human embryos.
stem cells [accept more specific answers like “embryonic stem cells” and “induced pluripotent stem cells”]

This author wrote a play based on the real life Helen Martins, who created The Owl House sculpture garden. In a play by this author, the photographer Styles takes a picture of the title character, who steals the identity of a dead man he finds in an alley so that he can remain in town. In a play this author developed with members of the The Serpent Players, John and Winston rehearse for a performance of Sophocles' Antigone while in an unnamed (*) prison. This author wrote a play in which the title character reminisces about flying a kite, while his Black servants Sam and Willie practice ballroom dancing. For 10 points, name this South African playwright of The Island and Master Harold... and the Boys.
Athol Fugard (The first two plays are The Road to Mecca and Sizwe Banzi Is Dead.)

This artist depicted the donor offering the altarpiece itself to St. Peter in his Stefaneschi Altarpiece. This artist's best-known work includes grisaille depictions of the seven virtues and vices, which run parallel to three fresco cycles depicting the lives of Christ, the Virgin, and Joachim. A building with a cobalt-blue ceiling houses a painting by this artist which depicts ten small (*) angels crying out in pain while darting around the title scene, his Lamentation. This student of Cimabue received his most famous commission from the penitent usurer Enrico Scrovegni. For 10 points, identify this early Renaissance artist who painted the Arena Chapel.

An author from this country wrote a trilogy of novels in which a ring is stolen from a general's grave. That author from this country later wrote about the adventures of the young boy Nils and the goose Martin. Another author from this country wrote a book featuring the evil knight Kato and the boy Mio, and penned a series about the freckled (*) Pippi Longstocking. In a play from this country, news that The Count is returning distresses the title character, who acquires a razor to commit suicide from the valet Jean. For 10 points, name this home country of the authors Selma Lagerlof, Astrid Lindgren, and August Strindberg.

This amino acid was used as an asymmetric catalyst in Benjamin List's 2021 Chemistry Nobel-winning aldol-condensation reaction. When subjected to the ninhydrin test, this amino acid is the only compound that produces yellow instead of purple. Unusually, peptide bonds involving this amino acid sometimes exist in the cis configuration. Vitamin C is a cofactor when this amino acid and glycine are (*) hydroxylated in the reaction to form collagen. This amino acid tends not to appear in alpha helices or beta-sheets due to steric hindrance of its side chain. For 10 points, name this only cyclic amino acid, denoted by the letter "P".

A simple Bayesian model of learning in these structures is named for DeGroot. Ronald Burt's "structural hole" theory equates social capital with non-redundancy in these structures. These structures exhibit "strong triadic closure" according to Mark Granovetter's paper "The Strength of Weak Ties." A 1967 experiment measured their average (*) path-length by asking people in Wichita and Omaha to forward letters to Boston. Stanley Milgram's small-world experiment estimated that there are "six degrees of separation" between any two nodes in, for 10 points, what systems of interpersonal connections, exemplified by Facebook?

A player of this instrument collaborated with Bill Evans on the 1962 album Undercurrent. The 1972 album Solo Flight contains nearly all the extant live recordings by a man who played this instrument in Benny Goodman's Sextet. The fourth track on Miles Davis' Bitches Brew is named for a player of this instrument who founded the group Mahavishnu Orchestra. This instrument, popularized by (*) Charlie Christian, was played by the composer of "Nuages" and "Minor Swing," who together with violinist Stephane Grappelli founded Paris's Quintette du Hot Club. For 10 points, Django Reinhardt played what stringed instrument?
jazz guitar (the artist in the first line is Jim Hall; the Miles Davis track is named after John McLaughlin.)

In integral domains named after this man, every ideal must necessarily be principal. Manifolds are defined as locally possessing a property named after this man. A theorem named after this man and Euler relates perfect numbers to Mersenne primes. An algorithm named after this man efficiently computes the (*) greatest common divisor of two integers. For 10 points, name this ancient Greek mathematician who wrote the Elements and who is considered the father of geometry.

A Michael Tooley essay about this practice imagines giving kittens a chemical that makes them develop human brains. Philippa Foot objected to this practice based on the doctrine of double effect in a paper which introduced the trolley problem, while Don Marquis argued against it because it deprives someone of a "future like ours." A "defense" of this practice by (*) Judith Jarvis Thomson imagines that you awaken to find your kidneys connected to a famous violinist. Some argue that this practice is permissible only up until "viability," or the ability to feel pain. For 10 points, name this practice which "pro-life" critics argue amounts to infanticide.

Louise Day Hicks founded an organization which opposed this practice known as Restore Our Alienated Rights, or ROAR. During protests over this practice in Boston, Stanley Forman took a Pulitzer Prize-winning photo of Joseph Rakes attacking Black lawyer Ted Landsmark with an American flag. Milliken v. Bradley set limitations on this practice which was ruled constitutional in (*) Swann v. Charlotte-Mecklenburg Board of Education. For 10 points, name this practice of transporting white students to non-white districts.

Note to players: Description acceptable. The victims of this event were defended in a report entitled Not Guilty written by a committee including John Dos Passos and Franz Boas that was chaired by John Dewey. Robert Conquest chronicled this event in his history The Great Terror. This event is often called the "doings" of Nikolai Yezhov, the newly appointed head of the (*) NKVD. During this period, the assassination of Sergei Kirov was used to falsely convict Zinoviev and Kamenev in the Trial of Sixteen. For 10 points, name this campaign of political repression carried out by Lenin's successor.
Joseph Stalin’s purges [or the Great Purge; accept the Moscow Show Trials; accept the Great Terror until mentioned; accept any answer that describes Joseph Stalin eliminating his political rivals]

One member of this family encouraged people to eat two meals a day during the "Arduous March." That man from this family was born in Russia as Yuri Irsenovich, but used his position as filmmaker to spread a legend that he had actually been born on a mountain with ritual significance. Another man from this family pioneered the songun policy of military primacy and the (*) Juche policy of self-reliance. That man ordered an invasion of his rival Syngman Rhee's nation, which surrounded Busan before being forced back to the Yalu river. That member of this family began his country's nuclear program. Kim [Accept Kim Jong-Il and Kim Il-Sung, do not accept any other specific Kim]

Two answers required. In an alternate version of Orion's death, he was struck with an arrow when one of these two deities bet the other that they could not hit him while he was swimming. Admetus won his wife Alcestis with help from one of these two deities, but then forgot to give offerings to the other. These two deities slew the giant Tityos after he assaulted a goddess pursued by the monster (*) Python. Niobe turned to stone after these two deities killed all 14 of her children. Since Hera prevented Leto from giving birth to these two deities on land, she gave birth on the floating island of Delos. For 10 points, name these twin deities, one a god of the sun and the other a goddess of the hunt.
Apollo and Artemis [accept Apollon or Phoebus in place of Apollo]

This country is home to many red and white cave paintings of animals in its Tsodilo Hills. Prehistoric stone tools have been found at Kubu Island in this nation, which sits in the middle of its Makgadikgadi salt pans. This country's northern city of Maun provides tourist access to the world's largest inland delta, the (*) Okavango. This country shares the world's only quadripoint with Zambia, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. For 10 points, what landlocked country that contains the majority of the Kalahari desert is located directly north of South Africa?

An approach to this discipline developed by Erving Goffman examines it through the lens of dramaturgy. Pragmatism inspired George Herbert Mead's theory of symbolic interactionism for this field. A book titled for the rules of this discipline's "method" defines it as the science of certain "facts." An early case study in this field suggested that greater anomie caused more (*) Protestants to perform one action than Catholics. This discipline founded by positivist Auguste Comte was promoted by the author of Suicide, Emile Durkheim. For 10 points, name this study of human society.

A ruler with this name had Alexander von Benckendorff lead the Third Section secret police. Sergei Witte drafted the October Manifesto after forces loyal to a king with this name killed protestors on Bloody Sunday. A king with this name was replaced by Alexander Kerensky's Provisional Government after the (*) February Revolution. Soldiers tried to replace a tsar of this name with his brother Konstantin in the Decembrist Revolt. Anna Anderson claimed to be Anastasia, the daughter of a tsar with this name killed by the Bolsheviks. For 10 points, give this name of the last Romanov tsar of Russia.

A full poetic transcreation of this work was done by P. Lal, while scholars at BORI synthesized its Critical Edition. After a character in this work realizes some water is actually a reflective floor, they mistake the nature of a pond and fall in. A woman's robe grows to protect herself after a character in this epic loses a rigged game. This epic about the (*) Kurukshetra ["koo-rook-SHEY-truh"] War contains the quote, "I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds." A section of this Vyasa ["vee-AAS-uh"] poem is a conversation between Krishna and Arjuna ["ar-JOO-nuh"]. For 10 points, name this Indian epic that includes the Bhagavad Gita ["BUH-guh-vud GHEE-tah"].

This poet wrote that "the distant strains of triumph / Burst agonized and clear" in a poem beginning, "Success is counted sweetest." This poet wrote of something that "sings the tune without the words / And never stops - at all" in one poem. This poet says, "I could not see to see" after a "Blue - uncertain stumbling (*) buzz" in another poem. This author of "Hope' is the thing with feathers" wrote that "The Carriage held but just Ourselves - / and Immortality" in another poem. For 10 points, name this poet of "I heard a Fly buzz - when I died" and "Because I could not stop for death."

In a play in this language, "Gotz of the Iron Hand" tells an Imperial trooper to "lick me on the behind." Count Maximilian of Moor's favorite son is disowned for becoming one of the title "robbers" in a play in this language. At a Walpurgis Night party, a character sees a vision of his love Gretchen in chains in a play exemplifying this language's (*) "Storm and Stress" period. Myths in this language inspired a play in which a scholar is trailed by a black poodle revealed to be Mephistopheles ["meh-fih-STAW-fih-leez"]. For 10 points, name this language used by Friedrich Schiller and Faust author Johann Wolfgang von Goethe ["GUR-tuh"].

In these materials, electrons are able to thermally populate the Fermi level despite the existence of a small band gap. A nanocrystal of one of these materials, such as cadmium selenide, makes up a quantum dot. Whether electrons or electron holes are the primary charge carriers in these materials determines if they are (*) n-type or p-type. Impurities are added to these materials in a process called doping. Germanium and silicon are examples of these materials used in integrated circuits. For 10 points, name these materials with conductivity between that of insulators and conductors.

In a novel set in this country, the jailer Atiq escorts a prostitute to her execution. That Yasmina Khadra novel is titled for The Swallows of [a city in this country]. The narrator of another novel from this country feels spring approaching after the orphan Sohrab gives off a lopsided smile. A servant from this country is told "For you, a (*) thousand times over!" after he is assaulted by the bully Assef. The Hazara boy Hassan performs the title action with Amir in that novel from this country. For 10 points, Khaled Hosseini's The Kite Runner depicts the rise of the Taliban in what country?
Afghanistan [or Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan] (the first two lines clue The Swallows of Kabul)

This composer inspired a Nathan Milstein piece titled after this composer and the suffix "-ana." In a piece by a different composer, an Andante cantabile ["ahn-DAHN-tay cahn-TAH-bee-lay"] D-flat major movement contains an inversion of a theme from a piece by this composer. A handbell used in this composer's second violin concerto inspired a "grand etude" ["AY-tood"] titled (*) "La campanella" by Franz Liszt. Sergei Rachmaninoff wrote a rhapsody based on an A minor piece by this composer that is often played as a virtuosic violin showpiece. For 10 points, name this Italian violinist and composer of 24 famous caprices ["cuh-PREE-sez"].
Niccolò Paganini [accept Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini or Grandes études de Paganini or Paganiniana]

Under Lukuas, some of these people burnt Alexandria during the Kitos ["KEE-toss"] War. A radical group of these people called the Sicarii committed mass suicide during a siege of the Masada fortress. Groups of these people formed the Zealots movement and were crushed by Hadrian in the (*) Bar Kokhba Revolt. Titus destroyed these people's Second Temple during a 70 AD siege. These people became subjects of the Roman Republic after the 63 BC sack of Jerusalem. For 10 points, name this persecuted religious group whose adherents make up most of the population of modern-day Israel.
Jewish people [or Jews or Roman Jews or people of Judea; accept Great Jewish Revolt; prompt on zealots until read]

This process is controlled by the presence of cis-regulatory elements such as enhancers and insulators. This process is initiated when the CAP ["cap"] protein binds to cyclic AMP ["A-M-P"] and attaches to the lac operon. The direction of this process is defined by the TATA ["tah-tah"] box. A molecule produced in this process is usually (*) modified with the addition of a 5-prime cap and poly-A tail, and its introns are removed by a splice•osome. In eukaryotes ["you-carry-oats"], this process is performed in the nucleus by RNA polymerase. For 10 points, name this process followed by translation, in which mRNA is created from a DNA template.

Note to players: Description acceptable. An instance of this action was preceded by the diversionary Battle of Iron Works Hill. The last occurrence of this action came right before Edward Hand's death near Assunpink Creek. After one instance of this action, Johann Rall was killed leading forces that had received warning it would occur. An image of this action showing (*) James Monroe holding a historically incorrect flag was made by Emanuel Leutze ["LOYT-zuh"]. Washington crossing the Delaware [prompt on attacking the Hessians or attacking the British or surprise attack by asking “What action preceded that attack?”; prompt on crossing a river by asking “What river was crossed?”]

This man became a national hero after defeating an expedition led by Isidro Barradas at the Battle of Tampico. After being wounded during the Pastry War, this man's leg was amputated and given a full military burial. An army led by this man lost the Battles of Buena Vista and Chapultepec. This man was caught wearing a private's uniform after he was beaten by (*) Sam Houston's army at the Battle of San Jacinto. Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna [or Antonio de Padua Maria Severino Lopez de Santa Anna y Perez de Lebron]

This river's flow was not properly controlled by the construction of the Sip Canal, which was itself flooded after the formation of Đerdap ["JAIR-dup"] Lake. Great War Island is located at the confluence of this river and the Sava River. During its flow through the Banat Mountains, this river travels through an extensive gorge system known as the (*) Iron Gates. Danube River [or Donau or Dunaj or Duna or Dunav or Dunărea or Doana]

This character's design by Ralph McQuarrie takes from a kabuto and a Stahlhelm. Ben Burtt used a scuba breathing apparatus to make this character's heavy breathing, not James Earl Jones. Darth Vader [or Lord Vader or Anakin Skywalker; prompt on Skywalker or Dark Lord]

This artist included the motto "as I can" in several paintings as a pun on his name. Art historian Erwin Panofsky claimed a work by this artist with scenes from the Passion of Christ was a visual contract. With his brother Hubert, this artist created a work that includes a stolen "Just Judges" panel and the (*) Adoration of the Mystic Lamb. This deity asked Alviss ["AHL-weess"] questions until the sun rose and turned him to stone. During Baldr's funeral, this deity kicked the dwarf Litr into the funeral pyre. This god was tricked into wrestling Elli, the personification of old age, by Utgard-Loki. Because a fly bit Brokkr's eyelid, part of a tool given to this god was (*) too short. This god disguised himself as the goddess Freya to retrieve that tool. At Ragnarok, this deity will kill Jormungandr ["YOUR-mun-gahn-der"] with a weapon that always returns after it is thrown. For 10 points, name this Norse god of thunder that wields Mjolnir ["mee-YOL-near"].

A 2009 rock song titled for this number urges the listener to "Lay down your arms, give up the fight." An artist whose name contains this number rhymes the line "I won't leave a breadcrumb" with the title, which references The Shining. In a song on Her Loss, an artist addressed by this number is asked "Can you talk to the (*) opps necks for me?" An artist who wrote "redrum" and featured on Drake's "Rich Flex" has this number in his name. A song by a duo named this number wishes "We could turn back time / To the good old days." For 10 points, "Stressed Out" is by a band named for how many "Pilots"?

The Schiff version of these substances is an aryl- or alkyl-substituted imine. Lithium di•iso•propyl•amide is an example of the "super" type of these substances. bases [or alkaline substances; accept strong bases or superbases or Schiff bases or Lewis bases or Bronstead-Lowry bases; accept nucleophiles until read; prompt on alkoxides]
